FR-001.title: An account carries a sign-in name, a first name, a last name, a display name, an employee number, a role and an active flag.

FR-002.title: A sign-in name is stored and matched in upper case, so signing in succeeds whatever case is typed.

FR-003.title: Accounts whose sign-in name is not upper case are migrated to that rule.
FR-003.tests: live check: sp_auth_credentials_check answered for a sign-in name typed upper, lower and mixed case after the upper-case comparison moved

FR-004.title: An employee number is exactly four digits and is deliberately not unique.

FR-005.title: A sign-in name, a first name and a last name are each 1 to 128 characters; the display name does not exceed 256.

FR-006.title: Creating a person writes the profile and the role assignment together.

FR-007.title: A new account is created active, and the create screen offers no active control.

FR-008.title: A duplicate sign-in name produces a definite already-taken answer that names the name and is never retried.

FR-009.title: A person is created with exactly one role and nothing adds a second; the stored assignments still permit more, so readers take the highest-ranked live role.

FR-010.title: The rank of every role is defined in one place and nowhere else.

FR-011.title: The retired administrator role is removed from the catalogue and replaced by IT Department.

FR-012.title: Every account that held the retired role moves onto IT Department in one all-or-nothing act.

FR-013.title: The change ships with a paired reversal that is run as part of verification.

FR-014.title: After the change no account has no role, and IT Department holds exactly the accounts that held the retired role.

FR-015.title: Material Handler Lead is added as a role in its own right with its own rank, not mapped onto Plant Manager.
FR-015.tests: live check of the shipped role seed against the local store (nine catalogue rows at their pinned rungs, admin at 0)

FR-016.title: The rank comparison and the roles-at-or-above list come from the one definition.

FR-017.title: Where a person holds more than one live role, the highest rank decides.

FR-018.title: The ladder leaves room between rungs and the rung of each role is checkable.

FR-019.title: A person cannot change an account whose role ranks strictly above their own, for the role, the active state, the sign-in name or the password.

FR-020.title: Peers remain editable, because a person's own rank is not above their own rank.

FR-021.title: A person's own account does not rank above them, so their own password change still works.

FR-022.title: A person cannot assign a role above their own rank, and the picker offers only roles at or below it.

FR-023.title: A person cannot deactivate their own account.

FR-024.title: A person cannot change the sign-in name of the account they are signed in as.

FR-025.title: The rank, self-lockout and sign-in-name rules are enforced where the change is written.

FR-026.title: A refused change is reported plainly and writes no audit record, because nothing changed.

FR-027.title: An account the reader cannot change is still readable, shows its fields and actions as unavailable, and states the reason.

FR-028.title: A password reset happens from a person's page, behind a confirmation, with no reset on the sign-in screen and none for oneself.

FR-029.title: A reset sets a random four-digit PIN, requires a change at the next sign-in, and does not reactivate a switched-off account.

FR-030.title: The reset PIN is shown once and is never readable back: only a salted hash may be stored, and 'read back' means plaintext.

FR-031.title: The value previously used for a reset stays recognised as a temporary value.

FR-032.title: A second reset replaces the earlier PIN and the screen says so.

FR-033.title: Creating a person issues a PIN the same way a reset does.

FR-034.title: The PIN window must be closed deliberately, is not dismissed by clicking outside or Escape, offers printing, and printing does not close it.

FR-035.title: A reset does not end an existing session for that person.

FR-036.title: After five failed sign-in attempts an account holding a temporary value stops accepting it.

FR-037.title: The count is held with the account, so closing and reopening the application does not clear it.

FR-038.title: The count does not expire with time.

FR-039.title: Only a successful sign-in or a fresh reset clears the count.

FR-040.title: The limit applies only to accounts holding a temporary value; ordinary sign-in keeps today's behaviour.

FR-041.title: Once an attempt has failed the remaining attempts are shown; they are not shown before one has.

FR-042.title: A failed sign-in for a sign-in name that does not exist behaves exactly as it does today.

FR-043.title: The wrong-attempt count is not presented as a record of who tried.

FR-044.title: When the count has been reached the person is told that someone entitled must issue a fresh reset.

FR-045.title: Every gated action is named by exactly one permission key, and a person either holds it or does not.

FR-046.title: The application holds one declaration of every permission with its key, label, what it gates, the area, the shipped fallback and the gate sites, and it carries no per-role baseline.

FR-047.title: A permission cannot exist without appearing on the page, nor appear without a baseline for every role; the declaration and the seeded baselines are checked in both directions.

FR-048.title: The shipped baselines are data rather than values fixed in code, so what a role may do can change without a code change.

FR-049.title: A permission resolves for the person: their own stored value, otherwise their role's baseline, otherwise the shipped fallback.

FR-050.title: An unreachable store yields the shipped fallback rather than a refusal.

FR-051.title: A new account starts from its role's baseline and holds nothing beyond it.

FR-052.title: The shipped baselines reproduce exactly what each role is allowed today, so nobody's access changes on ship day.

FR-053.title: A person's own stored value beats a wider scope, and the order is corrected and shipped before any value is stored for an individual.

FR-054.title: No gate decides access from a hand-written list of role names: all twelve lists the Context counts are removed, eleven replaced by their permission and the badge map re-keyed to role codes.

FR-055.title: A gate is refused wherever the gated action is performed, not only where the control was drawn.

FR-056.title: A control's visibility and the action it guards are answered from the same lookup.

FR-057.title: Whatever the Settings cache-refresh control admits is also admitted by the service's cache-refresh permission.

FR-058.title: The badge beside the signed-in name does not become a permission.

FR-059.title: The permission that opens and edits the permissions page cannot be changed from that page.

FR-060.title: A role added later is answered by its baseline or by the shipped fallback for every permission.

FR-061.title: A gated action reading a permission the declaration does not hold is reported as a failure rather than shipping as a silent refusal.

FR-062.title: A permission the declaration holds that no gate reads is reported.

FR-063.title: The permissions page shows one person at a time, is not a grid of roles against features, and changes no role's baseline.

FR-064.title: The permissions page is openable only by IT Department, Plant Manager and Developer.

FR-065.title: Each row states what the feature is, what it gates, the value in force, and whether it came from the role baseline or a choice for the person.

FR-066.title: A person whose role ranks above the reader's is selectable to view, with rows shown unavailable and the reason stated in words.

FR-067.title: Saving confirms what is changing and for whom, one sentence per changed row and a count when several change.

FR-068.title: Saving with nothing changed is unavailable and writes no history record.

FR-069.title: A completed save is reversible, and the reversal obeys the same rule as the change it reverses.

FR-070.title: A reversal does not overwrite a value that has moved; it shows what the value is now and asks before restoring.

FR-071.title: A reversal of a save that changed several rows reverses the whole save.

FR-072.title: Every permission change writes one history record per changed permission naming the actor, the permission, the scope, both values and the time.

FR-073.title: The page warns before it is left with unsaved changes and states how many rows are pending.

FR-074.title: The page shows pending changes as pending until they are saved.

FR-075.title: A second view answers which roles' baselines give a feature, taken from the seeded baselines the declaration's check ties to it rather than repeated.

FR-076.title: The same view names only the people who differ from their role's baseline, in either direction, each marked granted or denied.

FR-077.title: The view is read-only, and choosing a differing person opens that person's own page.

FR-078.title: A feature nobody holds is stated in words rather than shown as an empty region.

FR-079.title: A person who holds a feature but has been switched off is listed and marked as switched off.

FR-080.title: Settings gains an Administration category holding two entries, one opening the user list and one opening the permissions page.

FR-081.title: Each entry is shown by its own permission, and a reader entitled to neither does not see the category.

FR-082.title: Neither entry expands in place, and each carries a short description of what it opens.

FR-083.title: Leaving either page returns to Settings, and repeating a page does not walk back through repeats of it.

FR-084.title: Both entries are reachable from the Settings search.

FR-085.title: A page re-checks the reader's entitlement rather than staying open on a stale answer.

FR-086.title: The list searches sign-in name, display name, employee number and role.

FR-087.title: The list is filterable by role.

FR-088.title: The list shows everyone by default, with switched-off people clearly marked.

FR-089.title: The search and role filter are remembered for the person, and the page names the active filter and says how many people it is hiding.

FR-090.title: A filter that matches nobody is stated distinctly from there being no people at all.

FR-091.title: A saved filter that cannot be read causes everyone to be shown with the failure stated, never an empty list.

FR-092.title: A filter naming a role that no longer exists falls back to showing everyone and says the filter no longer applies.

FR-093.title: A row does exactly one thing, which is to open that person; reset, deactivate and reactivate live on that person's page.

FR-094.title: A row remains a single target, keeps all five facts visible at every width, and folds onto a second line rather than cropping.

FR-095.title: The list stays usable, and does not freeze while it loads, with a roster of 1,000 people.

FR-096.title: Where the store cannot be read the list shows an unavailable state with a retry, and never an empty list, a blank region or sample data.

FR-097.title: The page presents the fields in a form at the top and the actions in a clearly separated area below.

FR-098.title: A page the reader cannot act on says so at the top and shows its actions as unavailable rather than hiding them.

FR-099.title: The create page is a form only, with no actions area.

FR-100.title: An action chosen while edits are unsaved does not act on a half-edited person; the reader must save or discard first.

FR-101.title: A failed action keeps what the reader had and states what failed, and does not blank the page.

FR-102.title: Deactivating states both halves in one sentence, and the same sentence appears on the person's page.

FR-103.title: Reactivating states that access returns from the next sign-in.

FR-104.title: Saving is guarded against a repeated press, so one press creates exactly one person or writes exactly one change.

FR-105.title: The badge lookup is keyed on the role code and covers every role the catalogue holds.

FR-106.title: The fallback badge remains and is reachable only by a genuinely unknown or blank role.

FR-107.title: The vocabulary naming roles the catalogue has never held is removed rather than left in place.

FR-108.title: Every creation, change and password reset writes an audit record naming the actor, the field, both values and the time.

FR-109.title: The actor's name, employee number and role are recorded as they were at the time.

FR-110.title: One save changing several fields writes one record per changed field, sharing one identifier for the change.

FR-111.title: A password reset is recorded as having happened with no value on either side.

FR-112.title: Every label, title, field label, action and error message is localised through the application's resource mechanism.

FR-113.title: No control has a fixed width, and a long value wraps or trims with a tooltip rather than being cropped.

FR-114.title: No screen freezes or refuses interaction while it loads or saves.

FR-115.title: Every list remains usable with 1,000 rows.

FR-116.title: The screens remain usable between 150 and 200 percent scaling, and at the narrowest window the application permits.

FR-117.title: No control is shown to a person who cannot use it.

SC-001.title: For every key that replaces a retired list, and every person, the effective set on ship day equals exactly what that person's role was allowed before, with zero differences; the three keys with no predecessor are checked against their stated baseline sets.

SC-002.title: Zero hand-written role lists remain in the application, and adding one back is reported as a failure.

SC-003.title: Adding a new gated action without declaring its permission and every role's baseline is reported before it can ship as a silent refusal.

SC-004.title: Zero stored values for individual people are required for SC-001 to hold.

SC-005.title: After the role rename the count of accounts with no role is zero, and the set on IT Department equals the set that held the retired role.

SC-006.title: The paired reversal is executed as part of verifying this feature, and both comparisons hold again afterwards.

SC-007.title: A password reset hands over a credential that cannot be read back as plaintext anywhere in the application, its logs or the store.

SC-008.title: Five wrong tries with a temporary credential stop it working; a sixth correct attempt is refused; restarting and waiting do not restore it.

SC-009.title: A save changing N permissions writes exactly N records naming the acting user and both values, and reversing it restores all N.

SC-010.title: One impatient press of Save creates exactly one person, and one impatient press of a permission save writes exactly one change.

SC-011.title: Every screen is usable between 150 and 200 percent scaling and at the narrowest window, with all five facts of a list row visible at both widths.

SC-012.title: No screen freezes or refuses interaction while it loads or saves, verified against a live store.

SC-013.title: Changing a permission for one person takes effect for that person and changes no other person's effective set.

SC-014.title: For any chosen feature the who-holds-this view names every role whose baseline gives it, no role whose baseline does not, and only the people who differ.

SC-015.title: Every role in the catalogue shows its own badge, and the count of roles falling to the grey default is zero.

SC-016.title: A change to an account that outranks the actor is refused when attempted without the screen, for the role, the active state and the password alike.

SC-017.title: Opening either Administration page and returning to Settings takes one Back press, and the search reaches both entries.

SC-018.title: The full test suite passes with zero failures and the build is clean with zero warnings.
SC-018.tests: the whole suite and the clean solution build

SC-019.title: For every creation, change and password reset the audit names the actor as they were, carries one record per changed field, and shares one change identifier.

SC-020.title: Every string on this feature's screens renders from the shipped language resources, with no resource key ever shown to a person.

tasks.summary: 76 tasks across 12 phases and 37 waves; 60 parallel-safe; 24 foundational tasks carry the schema, the precedence re-rank, the permission declaration and the user-management data layer before any story starts.

specify.summary: Phase 2 finished (the bootstrap and its validators, the permission declaration, the role code through the session, permission resolution, the user-management data layer, registration, resource keys and the three wave-7 suites), and the first Phase 3 task landed: the shipped role seed now carries the eight rungs, Material Handler Lead and the name parts the schema requires.

implement.summary: Closed T072, T073, T074 and T075: the live integration pass now proves the create, the 1062 answer, a mid-way rollback, both rank and both self refusals, the reset's single empty audit row, deactivate leaving sessions alone, one change identifier per save and each person's ship-day parity; a reset's PIN was searched for across the store, the journal and the application and found nowhere; the suite and a clean build are green; and the running application was walked, which found and fixed an unreachable create form and a hidden count that never moved. T076 is open.

T001.did: Recorded the settings scope census (3 rows, all all_users) and the admin account set (test.admin) as fixture data

T002.did: Captured the twelve retired role lists verbatim, with administrator and Setup Tech recorded as matching no catalogue role

T003.did: Added first_name, last_name and temporary_credential_failed_attempts to core_users_profiles; scratch-database run proved the guarded rollback drops exactly those three

T004.did: Added role_rank INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with an index to auth_roles_catalog; longest index name 31 characters

T005.did: Created auth_user_management_audit at 32_ with the 12 declared columns and no foreign keys, so the actor snapshots outlive the accounts they name

T006.did: Re-ranked fn_config_settings_scope_rank to computer 1, all_users 2, role 3, admin 4, developer 5, user 6; scratch-database run read back 1,2,3,4,5,6 and the rollback restored 1,2,3,4,5 with role 0

T008.did: Added role_code and the wrong-attempt count to the three credential reads, plus the upper-case sign-in-name contract in their headers; all three recreate and return the documented ordinal order against a scratch store

T009.did: Added sp_auth_temporary_credential_attempt_record (one statement per branch, non-query) and the header comment on sp_config_settings_upsert recording why it is not the permission write path and why ELSE 'developer' stays

T010.did: Added the roster read (four-field search, optional role filter, everyone and switched-off people by default) and the one-person read returning identity, rung, active flag and attempt count; both exercised against a scratch store

T011.did: Added the create procedure: one transaction writing profile plus exactly one role assignment; proved rank refusal, unknown-role refusal, pass-through 1062 and eight audit rows sharing one change group

T012.did: Added the update procedure: target-rank refusal checked before the requested-role refusal, self-deactivate and self-rename refusals, and audit rows only for fields that actually changed (nothing-changed wrote none)

T013.did: Added the reset procedure: stores the salted hash only, forces a change, clears the attempt count, leaves is_active as it was, ends no session, and writes one audit row with both value columns null; target-rank refusal and a null-value audit row both proved

T014.did: Added sp_config_permissions_user_get keyed on scope_key, resolving the role inside the procedure and returning only permission-namespace rows; proved it returns the person's own row and their role's row and excludes another role's baseline and a text preference

T015.did: Added the sign-in-name upper-case migration with a recorded backup table its rollback restores then drops; proved against a scratch store that it upper-cases, records one row, reports rather than fails, and that the rollback restored the original spelling

T007.did: Bootstrap update path carries guarded adds for the three person columns, role_rank and its index, plus the new audit table; new user_management_schema validator added and settings validator asserts the corrected rank order; applied to the live local mtm_waitlist (columns and table landed, re-run reports already exists, exit 0) and a scratch full-schema build validates at 0 issues on all three validators

T016.did: One declaration: the fourteen pinned keys as constants plus per-key label/gates resource keys, area, shipped fallback and gate sites; no per-role baseline carried; solution builds 0 warnings 0 errors

T017.did: StartupState carries the signed-in person's role code and id, the code is threaded through StartupCredentialCheckResult, StartupSessionSnapshot and StartupPasswordResetRequirement, StartupState.IsDeveloper now reads the role code and not the display name, and the coordinator plus the sign-in view model are the producers that set both; solution builds 0 warnings 0 errors

T018.did: Permission resolution for one person: own stored row, then the role baseline, then the shipped fallback, composed from one read of sp_config_permissions_user_get, cached per person with explicit invalidation, undeclared keys throw rather than refusing silently, and an unreachable store answers from the fallback; solution builds 0 warnings 0 errors

T019.did: User-management service and repository behind the six procedures: identity rules and the 256-bounded derived display name applied in the service, the actor taken from the signed-in state, the 1062 duplicate and each mtm_* refusal turned into one typed reason in the repository, every write through the non-query seam, no statement text; live store proof of the create path (profile + one assignment + 7 field audit rows + 1 null-value credential row, actor snapshotted) and of the pinned 1062 answer, both cleaned up afterwards

T020.did: Sign-in repository stores and compares sign-in names in upper case, carries the role code and wrong-attempt count through all three credential reads with the caller ordinals moved, records a temporary-credential attempt through the new procedure outside the retry so one try moves the count once, and enforces the five-attempt limit before comparing the value; verified live - the three reads answer for a name typed upper, lower and mixed case, the count moves to 2 and clears to 0, and all 75 procedures applied to the live store with 0 failures

T021.did: PermissionService, IUserManagementRepository/UserManagementRepository and IUserManagementService/UserManagementService registered in the composition root; the registration class is partial with RegisterUserManagementPages, RegisterUserAccountPages and RegisterPermissionsPages declared and called; solution builds 0 warnings 0 errors

T022.did: Resource keys for the whole feature: 28 permission label/gates keys generated from the declaration's own key names, the nine Role_<role_code> display texts, the Administration category pair, the roster, create, person, PIN, permissions and who-holds-this strings, and the thirteen UserManagement_Outcome keys the service resolves; file parses, 454 keys total, no duplicate key, every key the code resolves is present

T023.did: All four roll-ups plus AllViews regenerated from the artifact folders; installed into a scratch schema in the installer's own order and every one applied cleanly, all three validators report 0 issues, and the installed counts match the folders (22 tables, 75 procedures, 3 functions, 2 views). Found and fixed a pre-existing fresh-store defect on the way: seed_config_image_storage_settings truncated a table another table holds a foreign key to, which stopped the whole seed phase; the truncate is now guarded

T026.did: Every suite that built a state for the developer check now sets the role code: CoreModelsTests (the display name is proved to decide nothing), StartupModelsTests, StartupOptionsModelsTests, ControlInspectorServiceTests, TooltipServiceTests and StartupCoordinatorTests. SplashViewModelTests needed no change - it constructs a bare StartupState and never sets a role, checked rather than assumed. Suite green: 1181 total, 0 failed, 1154 passed, 27 skipped

T025.did: Permission resolution and the precedence trap asserted: a role baseline is inherited, a person's own row beats it in either row order, a role with no baseline answers from the fallback, a store that throws answers from the fallback, an undeclared key reports a failure, several keys are answered from one store read, the cache holds for the session and drops on invalidate and on a sign-in that resolves a different person; SettingsScopeRankTests asserts the six rungs and the corrected order by reading the shipped function artifact. 24 new cases, all pass

T027.did: The shipped role seed gives every live role its rung (developer 100, plant_manager 80, production_lead 70, setup_lead 60, material_handler_lead 50, the three worker roles 10), adds Material Handler Lead as a role in its own right, leaves the retired admin row unranked in its own statement so it holds the column default 0, and now supplies first_name and last_name on every seeded account; the rollback removes exactly the row it added. Applied to the live local store: the nine catalogue rows read back at those rungs with admin at 0, and no account is missing its name parts. The fresh-store aggregate install now runs its whole seed phase cleanly

T024.did: Ran PermissionRegistryTests against the live-store environment: 10/10 passed, so the declaration half T024 still owns holds; the baseline comparison stays in T034

T028.did: Added sp_auth_roles_list with create.sql and rollback.sql, applied to live MySQL 5.7 and read back: 8 rows ordered by rung desc then code, retired admin row excluded while still present in the catalogue

T029.did: Added RoleAuthorization (IsAtLeast, IsAbove, AtOrAbove, AtOrBelow, Highest over catalogue entries) plus IRoleCatalogService and RoleCatalogService reading sp_auth_roles_list with a session cache; registered in the composition root; clean solution build 0 warnings 0 errors

T030.did: Regenerated AllSPs.sql with a UTF-8-safe generator: +37 lines for sp_auth_roles_list only, 76 of 76 procedure artifacts present verbatim and the rebuild is byte-identical. AllSeeds.sql left unchanged because feature 006's seed revision is already present verbatim; its two drifted blocks belong to other features and were reported instead of silently rewritten

T031.did: Phase 3 ladder suite exists and passes against the live store: 23 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped across RoleAuthorizationTests, RoleCatalogServiceTests and RoleLadderSeedTests, including the live nine-code catalogue check.

T032.did: Rename seed written with a transactional procedure and an EXIT HANDLER that rolls back and resignals; AllSeeds.sql regenerated from the folders and proved by building a scratch store from the aggregates, which ends with it_department at rung 90, admin absent, one account on the renamed role and zero accounts holding no role.

T033.did: Live proof ran the shipped create.sql, rolled it back with the shipped rollback.sql and re-applied it: the accounts on IT Department equal the set that held admin, no account holds no role at any of the three points, a switched-off fixture moved and stayed switched off, and the run ends with it_department at rung 90 and admin absent.

T067.did: RoleBadgeCatalog added: one entry per role the catalogue holds, each with its own glyph and colour, the grey default reachable only by a genuinely unknown or blank role, and the retired vocabulary plus the display-name branches removed. Glyphs are drawn only from codepoints this application already renders.

T068.did: ShellViewModel's badge now reads RoleBadgeCatalog.For(role code) instead of its own switch over display names, so the badge is answered by the one lookup and stays presentation rather than becoming a permission.

T069.did: RoleBadgeCatalogTests proves the lookup covers every role the shipped seeds write, that the count reaching the grey default is zero, that each role's glyph and colour are distinct, that the retired vocabulary and display names reach the default, and that the badge is not a permission; ShellViewModelTests proves the shell reads the lookup and keeps no retired branch. 33 passed, 0 failed.

T064.did: The sign-in view model shows the remaining attempts once an attempt has failed and never before, says a fresh reset is needed when the limit has been reached, clears the line on a successful sign-in, and keeps an ordinary account and an unknown sign-in name exactly as they were; the sign-in page carries the line through x:Load with a stable AutomationId and offers no reset. Two resource keys added under Startup_SignIn.

T065.did: Sign-in view-model cases added: the line appears after the first failure and not before, the reached-the-limit wording names a reset by somebody entitled, an account without a temporary credential keeps today's hint and shows no line, and the sign-in page carries the bound line with no reset offered. 22 tests in the file pass.

T066.did: Live end-to-end proof added: five wrong attempts stop the temporary credential, the sixth attempt with the correct value is refused, the count survives a new repository instance, nothing in the path computes a window so waiting cannot restore it, a successful sign-in clears it, the legacy 0000 marker is limited the same way, an unknown sign-in name moves no count, a failed attempt writes no audit row, a reset clears the count and issues a working value that supersedes the old PIN, and a reset leaves an open session running. 9 tests pass against the live store. Finding: the repository recorded every failed attempt against user id 0, so the count never moved and the limit never bit; the resolved account id now travels beside the verdict.

T036.did: Seeded one role-scoped bool row per permission per role (14 keys x 9 roles = 126 rows), keyed role:<role_code> in the permission namespace; proved live against MAMP MySQL 5.7 (126 rows, 14 keys, 9 roles, subset rule settings.cache_refresh subset of cache.refresh_api holds, zero user-scoped rows); AllSeeds.sql regenerated from the folders and holds exactly one copy of the new body.

T034.did: Wrote the baseline parity test (per role and per permission against the twelve retired lists, the three stated no-predecessor keys, the declaration-vs-baseline check in both directions, the stated material_handler_lead row and zero per-person rows) and the service-host subset test (settings.cache_refresh admits nobody the cache.refresh_api baseline refuses, declared gate site, fail-closed fallback, retired operator list preserved). 11/11 pass.

T037.did: Re-closed with the full change: the composition root now names the new permissionService parameter on WaitlistViewViewModel (WaitlistViewRegistrationTests.ListViewModelRegistration_NamesEveryConstructorParameter caught the omission, which is the guard working). Solution builds 0 errors; full suite 1282 total / 1244 passed / 38 skipped / 0 failed against the live MAMP store.

T038.did: The service host's role list is gone: the API now answers permission.cache.refresh_api for the caller's own id, read from mtm_waitlist and composed by the same StoredPermissionAnswers the client app uses. Live proof: developer id 1 resolves 1, setup id 8 resolves 0, identity read returns id/role_code for TEST.DEVELOPER.

T039.did: The Settings screen's four lists, its two Administration entries, the minutes editor, the defect-type catalogue and the computer registry now read named permissions. SettingsViewModel is INavigationAware and loads all eight answers in one call in OnNavigatedTo (the repository's own navigation-aware pattern), handing the two child view models their answers; every gate stays false until its answer arrives. Four Settings suites rewritten to state permissions instead of role names; the reflection lookup that named the deleted arrays is gone. Settings module: 277 passed, 11 skipped, 0 failed.

T040.did: Dunnage Quick Add now reads permission.setup.dunnage_quick_add and work-centre setup reads permission.setup.work_centers; the Setup Tech entry that matched no catalogue role is gone, so a plain Setup person is no longer given work-centre setup by default. SetupWorkCenterViewModel loads its one answer in OnNavigatedTo (navigation-aware, the repo's own pattern) and the management controls stay hidden until it arrives; the service gate refuses at the action in the same words. Setup module: 60 passed, 16 skipped, 0 failed.

T035.did: The gate-site audit lands green and lands LAST, as the sequencing rule requires: it enumerates all thirteen sites from the spec's Context (twelve retired lists in nine files plus StartupState.IsDeveloper in a tenth), reads the nine role display names from the shipped Resource.resw rather than restating them, reads the keys from the declaration, and fails on a role-name array in any production .cs file or on a gate asking for an undeclared key. 7/7 pass, so 'no gate reads its own role list' is now provably true.

T041.did: Ran the audit, the parity test and the subset test together: 18 passed, 0 failed. decisions.decision: sp_config_permissions_user_get matches on scope_key (user:ID and role:CODE) rather than on the user_id column. Why: the data model pins scope_key as the keying, so the read does not depend on a second column being populated by whoever writes the row, and a user_id-keyed form was proved to miss a correctly keyed row. Rejected: keying on user_id on the assumption the writer always fills it.

sp_user_management_update checks the target rung before the requested role rung. Why: a reader editing somebody who outranks them must be told that, not told they cannot assign the role. The second refusal is true but describes the smaller half of the problem, and the page states the first. Rejected: checking the requested role first, which returned mtm_rank_denied for an outranking target.

The account-change audit table carries no foreign keys. Why: actor_user_id and target_user_id must outlive the accounts they name, so a constraint would contradict the snapshot rule and block the hard delete of a person the audit talks about. Rejected: foreign keys mirroring auth_roles_assignments.

seed_username_upper_normalization records originals in a backup table that its rollback drops. Why: upper-casing destroys the original spelling, so reversibility needs it recorded, and the table is not a permanent schema artifact so it needs no AllTables entry. Rejected: a rollback that cannot restore case because nothing was recorded.

Writing an account initial credential in sp_user_management_create also writes an audit row with both value columns null. Why: it keeps one rule for a credential being set across create and reset, and the PIN is never stored so there is no before or after value to record (FR-111). Rejected: omitting the row, which would leave create and reset recording the same act two different ways.
T007 leaves Database/Bootstrap/create_database.sql without DDL and only documents the fresh-store path in its header.
decisions.why: That file drops and recreates the database, so it can never be part of the update path, and a fresh store gets its table shape from Database/Tables/**/create.sql (rolled up in AllTables.sql) with the guarded additions in update_table_descriptions.sql running last. Putting the same DDL in it as well would have been two owners for one shape, and dead statements on the only path that reads it.
decisions.rejected: Duplicating the column and table DDL in create_database.sql, which the task text named alongside update_table_descriptions.sql.

decisions.decision: UserManagementRepository opens its own MySqlConnection for reads and writes instead of going through IMySqlHelperServer.
decisions.why: The helper server answers a failed call with its neutral result, which would fold a duplicate sign-in name into a generic failure and would hand an unreachable store on as an empty roster. Both requirements need the provider own answer: the pinned 1062 for a duplicate, and a loud failure so an empty list is never shown for an outage.
decisions.rejected: Reading and writing through IMySqlHelperServer and inferring the cause from an empty result.

decisions.decision: One shipped fallback rule: permission.requests.handle answers true, the other thirteen answer false.
decisions.why: An unreachable store must not turn every control into a refusal (FR-050), and it must not hand out anything new either. Exactly one key is operationally load-bearing while the store is down, so the shop floor keeps working and nobody gains administration.
decisions.rejected: Answering true everywhere, which would grant administration during an outage, and answering false everywhere, which would stop the floor from accepting requests.

decisions.decision: PasswordSecretHasher holds the one implementation of the credential hashing, used by the sign-in path and the reset path.
decisions.why: A reset writes a credential the sign-in path has to accept. Two copies of PBKDF2 with the same constants would let a change in one make every PIN issued from the other silently unusable, and nothing in the build or the suite could see it.
decisions.rejected: Keeping the private hashing helpers in StartupSessionRepository and a second copy in the user-management service.

decisions.decision: The temporary-credential attempt count is moved outside the sign-in retry wrapper.
decisions.why: The read runs under a bounded retry, and a retry that re-ran the count would add a second failure for one try. One press of Sign in must move the count exactly once.
decisions.rejected: Recording the attempt inside the retried lambda.

decisions.decision: The role seed writes the retired admin row in its own INSERT that omits role_rank.
decisions.why: A shared column list cannot omit the column for one row and supply it for the rest, and the task requires the row to be left unranked so it holds the column default. The role rename reads that rung back when it reverses, so writing an explicit 0 would quietly change what the reversal claims to restore.
decisions.rejected: One INSERT carrying an explicit 0 for admin.

decisions.decision: The permission registry declares no per-role baseline and a test asserts the type has no member for one.
decisions.why: FR-046 and FR-048 split the two tiers on purpose: baselines are seeded data so what a role may do changes without a code change. The check is visible in the type rather than only in a comment about where the data lives.
decisions.rejected: Carrying a baseline table on the declaration, which the seed contradiction suggested and the research settled against.

decisions.decision: The permission baselines are seeded as role-scoped rows keyed role:<role_code>, one per permission per role, in the same config_settings_values shape sp_config_permissions_user_get matches on
decisions.why: The declaration must not carry per-role baselines (FR-046/FR-048) and the read already matches on scope_key rather than on user_id
decisions.rejected: A per-role dictionary inside PermissionRegistry, which would have put the answers back in code

decisions.decision: material_handler_lead's whole row is stated rather than compared against a retired list: it holds requests.handle, cache.refresh_api, admin.users and admin.reset_password, and nothing else
decisions.why: Phase 3 added the role after the twelve lists were captured, so no list can describe it; the specification's Assumptions state it and explicitly deny it ignored_locations
decisions.rejected: Deriving it from the worker roles' union, which would have granted ignored_locations against the specification

decisions.decision: RequestActionPolicy keeps its pure status and assignee rules and takes the handler answer as an input, but the answer itself is now the named permission
decisions.why: Deleting the eight-name list is what FR-054 asks for, and the policy stays unit-testable because it never resolves the permission itself
decisions.rejected: Making the whole policy asynchronous and store-backed

decisions.decision: WaitlistViewDetailViewModel's dead role field was deleted rather than turned into a permission reader
decisions.why: It was assigned from StartupState and read nowhere, and the detail page carries no action gates; a reader there would be a wrapper with no decision behind it
decisions.rejected: Adding an unused permission read so the file would appear in the audit's gate-site list

decisions.decision: induce the mid-way create failure by holding the role-assignment table's rows and gaps in another transaction while the create runs
decisions.why: every refusal the create's inputs can provoke is raised before the profile insert, so no input reaches a failure after it, and proving the rollback needed a failure that really lands mid-way
decisions.rejected: reporting a lock wait or a first-write failure as if it were the mid-way case

decisions.decision: write the update procedure's two active flags as literals instead of CAST(... AS CHAR)
decisions.why: a CAST takes the connection's collation while the routine's variables take the database's, and MySQL 5.7 refuses to union the two, so the save failed on every call from a utf8mb4 connection
decisions.rejected: forcing a collation with COLLATE, which pins the store to one collation name

decisions.rejected: reaching the create form from the person's page instead, which the contract does not ask for

decisions.rejected: leaving it, since the count is what FR-094 promises

concerns.note: The database contract requires BEGIN ... END procedure bodies with an EXIT HANDLER, and no procedure in this repo had ever needed one. The mysql client splits a script on the semicolon, so every compound body must ship DELIMITER blocks or the CREATE fails with 1064 while the script still looks like it ran. Fixed here; recorded because the next compound procedure will hit it.

The case-insensitive utf8mb4_unicode_ci collation makes the naive form of the upper-case migration a silent no-op: col not-equal-to UPPER(col) is false because the two sides compare equal. The migration now forces BINARY on every comparison. Caught only by running it.

T008 appended columns to the three credential reads and their caller reads by ordinal. Applying these SQL artifacts to a store before T020 moves the caller ordinals breaks sign-in. Neither the build nor the suite can see this, because index-based reads compile.

The shipped baseline seed Database/Seeds/seed_dev_masked_baseline/create.sql inserts into core_users_profiles without first_name or last_name. Both are NOT NULL with no default, so the seed fails once T003 is applied. T027 owns that file and must add the two values.

FR-005 allows first_name and last_name at 128 characters each and the display name at 256. Two maximum-length names derive a 257-character display name, which the VARCHAR(256) column rejects. The derivation must be bounded in the caller (T019, T047); nothing in the store can rescue it.

The scratch-database proofs of T003 to T015 ran through an ad-hoc PowerShell harness against a scratch schema, not through a repository command, so they are recorded as an account rather than as machine-verified evidence. No live store was written to.

T024 asserts the declaration in both directions against the seeded baselines, but those baselines do not exist until T036 writes them in Phase 5. The declaration half is implemented and green (permission registry, pinned spellings, gate sites, resource keys); the declaration-versus-baseline half cannot be written before the seed it compares against. T024 is left open, and the baseline direction belongs with T034 and T036.

T022 asks for every resource key for the whole feature, and six screens do not exist until Phases 6 to 10. The keys the feature already names are present, including 28 permission strings, nine role displays, the Administration pair, the roster, the create form, the person page, the PIN window, the permissions page, the who-holds-this view and the thirteen outcome messages the service resolves. A later phase that finds its screen needs another string adds it to the same map, which is the single place the ownership rule wanted.

Two paths read the signed-in role name and compare it to role names and are owned by no task Files line: MTM_Waitlist.Waitlist.View/ViewModels/WaitlistViewViewModel.cs and WaitlistViewDetailViewModel.cs pass the role name into RequestActionPolicy, and MTM_Waitlist.Waitlist.View/Services/WaitlistRequestService.cs calls the same policy to enforce at the action. T037 replaces the policy with permission.requests.handle and names only the policy file, so those three call sites move with it or the handle gate is only half replaced.

sp_user_management_create commits its own transaction internally, so an outer START TRANSACTION and ROLLBACK around it does not undo it. T072 live check must make the procedure fail mid-way to prove the rollback rather than wrapping the call in a transaction. Found by running the create path against the live store and finding the probe row still present after an outer rollback.

Database/Seeds/seed_config_image_storage_settings/create.sql truncated a table that config_settings_history holds a foreign key to, which stopped the whole seed phase of a fresh install at that file. Fixed with the same FOREIGN_KEY_CHECKS guard the table artifacts use. The file belongs to no task in this feature and was found by installing the regenerated aggregates.

A fresh store built from the aggregates holds 23 base tables against 22 table artifact folders. The extra one is seed_username_case_backup, created by the username-normalisation seed as a migration-lifetime table with no folder of its own, which its own header states. Not a defect; a count check has to know about it.

MySQL Server 9.6.0 is what the live store runs on while every artifact header still says Engine: MySQL 5.7. Nothing in this feature needed a version-specific behaviour, and the compound procedure bodies and the guarded bootstrap blocks ran unchanged, but the headers are now inaccurate.

Root cause of the one suite failure, established by hand against the live store: mtm_receiving_application does not carry the Database/MTMReceivingApp artifacts. receiving_history has no part_type column and sp_receiving_history_average_coil_weight does not exist, so the coil test's insert and its procedure call both fail, and MySqlHelperServer turns both into an empty result after exhausting its retries rather than throwing, which is why the failure reads as Expected 1 Actual 0 instead of as a database error. Not caused by feature 006: nothing in this round touches that database, that tree or that test. It needs the receiving-app artifacts applied to the fresh install before that gate can be green.

Because the raw-SQL seam returns an empty result when the store refuses, a live test that expects rows cannot tell a missing procedure from an empty answer. That masking is worth knowing about when reading any live failure in this suite.

T037's task text says WaitlistViewDetailViewModel and WaitlistRequestService each compare a role name today. Neither does: the detail view model holds a dead role field and the request service compared only status and assignee. The service was given a real permission refusal, which is what the task wanted, and the dead field was deleted. The task list overstates the pre-change state.

The four Settings gates and SetupWorkCenterViewModel.CanManageWorkCenters are synchronous XAML-bound properties computed from StartupState.CurrentRole. Replacing them with permissions needs an asynchronous load whose results the bindings read, and SettingsViewModel is not navigation-aware and has no asynchronous init hook, so T039 and T040 need a page-lifecycle decision the task list does not make. Left open rather than half-migrated.

T038 cannot be contained in Api/ServiceOperatorRoles.cs as its Files line says: the gate needs the caller's user id, so IServiceOperatorRoleResolver, ServiceOperatorRoleResolver, ServiceOperatorAuthenticationHandler, ServiceHostBuilder and the Mock.Service test doubles all have to move with it. Left open.

MTM_Waitlist.Tests/Module_Startup/Services/TemporaryCredentialLimitTests.cs carries four CS8602 warnings from round 3, so the solution builds with four warnings rather than none. Not fixed this round.

T076 is open and was not walked. The 150 and 200 percent scaling walks need the session's display scale changed, which needs a sign-out, and this pass ran unattended; the narrowest-window walk needs the shell and the application could not be signed back in through UI Automation afterwards. What the markup reading found is recorded in quickstart.md, explicitly as a reading rather than as evidence.

The hidden-count fix is a markup change verified by the build and by the pre-fix observation of the defect, not re-observed in the running application, because the session could not be signed in again after the walk's own sign-out.

The account JKOLL (user 2) was reset by accident while the T073 search harness was being written: an early bug in the harness read a scalar as its first character and performed the reset against user id 2 instead of the probe fixture. The account now holds a temporary credential with a fresh change required, and one audit row records that reset (deliberately left in place rather than deleted). The developer account JOHNK now holds a real salted password equal to the value this workstation already remembered for it, because the walk drove the application's own change-password form.

T072's task line names three test files, but several of the live claims it lists (the transactional create, the 1062 answer through the repository, the rank refusals, the self-lockout refusals, the reset audit row, deactivate leaving sessions alone) had no live case at all; they were added in a new live suite rather than asserted from the fakes.

last_action: T072, T073, T074 and T075 closed with evidence recorded in quickstart.md; T076 left open and the spec left at implementing, because the scaling walk needs a session the pass could not make
